sentences.zh: 在竞选活动中，唐纳德·特朗普和卡玛拉·哈里斯不断谈论贸易、关税和国内制造业。

sentences.en: Now people are moving their companies to other countries.

sentences.en: And we will ensure that the next generation of breakthroughs are not only invented, but built right here in America by American union workers.
sentences.zh: 我们将确保下一代突破性技术不仅在美国发明，而且由美国工会工人在美国本土制造。

sentences.en: That's because, in many ways, the United States is still reeling from a single trade deal that transformed the U.S.

sentences.en: economy and remade both parties' relationship to the working class.
sentences.zh: 经济并重塑了两个政党与工人阶级的关系。

sentences.en: Today, Times Magazine writer Dan Kaufman with the story of how the North American Free Trade Agreement broke American politics.
sentences.zh: 今天，《时报杂志》撰稿人丹·考夫曼将讲述北美自由贸易协定是如何打破美国政治的故事。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月8日，星期二。

sentences.en: Dan, it's a pretty rare thing when we can trace the origins of our politics back to something really concrete and specific, not, you know, a set of vast intangible forces,
sentences.zh: 丹，当我们能够将我们政治的根源追溯到非常具体和确切的事情，而不是那些你知道的庞大且无形的无形力量时，这真的是一件非常罕见的事，

sentences.en: but a moment in time when a group of people got together and made a decision.
sentences.zh: 而是一群人聚在一起做出决定的那一刻。

sentences.en: And you contend that to understand our politics today, specifically to understand this presidential campaign, you can go back to one such decision made in the 1990s around U.S.
sentences.zh: 你认为要理解我们今天的政治，特别是要理解这次总统竞选，你可以追溯到20世纪90年代围绕美国做出的这样一个决定。

sentences.en: trade policy.

sentences.en: So just explain that and justify it.
sentences.zh: 所以请解释一下并证明这一点。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, in 1993, Congress passed the North American Free Trade Agreement, NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 1993年，国会通过了《北美自由贸易协定》，即NAFTA。

sentences.en: It was signed into law by Bill Clinton.
sentences.zh: 它由比尔·克林顿签署成为法律。

sentences.en: What it did was it opened up trade with Mexico and Canada.
sentences.zh: 它的作用是打开了与墨西哥和加拿大的贸易。

sentences.en: And I think it was one of the most pivotal political moments.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最具决定性的政治时刻之一。

sentences.en: It signaled the outsourcing of good-paying manufacturing jobs, particularly in the Rust Belt states, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 它标志着高薪制造业岗位的流失，特别是在铁锈带州：威斯康星州、密歇根州、宾夕法尼亚州、俄亥俄州。

sentences.en: But it also signaled something much more long-term and transformative.
sentences.zh: 但它也标志着更长远、更具变革意义的事情。

sentences.en: And I think that is a political shift with the Democratic Party moving away from its working-class New Deal roots towards the professional class and wealthier.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是民主党的政治转变，从其工人阶级的新政根基转向了专业阶层和更富裕阶层。

sentences.en: Towards the college-educated.
sentences.zh: 转向受过大学教育的人。

sentences.en: College-educated and wealthier, including a lot of people on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 受过大学教育且更富裕的人，包括华尔街的很多人。

sentences.en: And the Republican Party, which had traditionally been the party of big business, at least rhetorically embracing a working-class politics,
sentences.zh: 而传统上作为大企业政党的共和党，至少在言辞上拥抱了工人阶级政治，

sentences.en: whether or not they fulfilled any of those promises is another question.
sentences.zh: 至于他们是否兑现了这些承诺则是另一个问题。

sentences.en: But the rhetoric changed markedly.
sentences.zh: 但言辞发生了显著的变化。

sentences.en: In other words, NAFTA is a moment where our basic understandings and assumptions about how the two parties relate to this really huge
sentences.zh: 换句话说，北美自由贸易协定是一个时刻，我们对这两个政党如何与这个极其庞大

sentences.en: and always symbolically significant segment of the population, the working class, the people who work in factories, people who make things.
sentences.zh: 且在象征意义上始终重要的人口群体——工人阶级、工厂工人、制造产品的人——的基本理解和假设。

sentences.en: It changes, and it kind of shatters.
sentences.zh: 它发生了改变，并且在某种程度上破碎了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It realigned the parties.
sentences.zh: 它重新洗牌了各政党。

sentences.en: And I think those dynamics are still playing out today.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些动态在今天仍在继续发挥作用。

sentences.en: So, Dan, take us back to the time and the place and the debate that brought us NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 那么，丹，带我们回到带来北美自由贸易协定的那个时代、地点和辩论中去。

sentences.en: And I should say, I vaguely remember it, because I think it was pretty much the first big public policy debate that occurred in my young adulthood.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，我依稀记得，因为我认为这几乎是我成年初期发生的第一场大型公共政策辩论。

sentences.en: CNN was kind of a mainstay in my childhood living room.
sentences.zh: 有线电视新闻网（CNN）是我童年客厅里的顶梁柱。

sentences.en: And I can remember some of this, but very vaguely.
sentences.zh: 我还能记得其中的一些，但非常模糊。

sentences.en: So plunge us back into it.
sentences.zh: 所以请带我们深入其中。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, the debate over NAFTA emerged at a kind of interesting, difficult moment in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 关于北美自由贸易协定的辩论出现在20世纪70年代一个有趣且困难的时刻。

sentences.en: There was a period of high inflation and then high interest rates, and this eventually led to two recessions.
sentences.zh: 那是一个高通胀随后高利率的时期，这最终导致了两场经济衰退。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That is the context in which Ronald Reagan first floats in 1979, this idea of a North American free trade agreement.
sentences.zh: 这就是罗纳德·里根在1979年首次提出建立北美自由贸易协定这一想法的背景。

sentences.en: And what was the logic of it?
sentences.zh: 那背后的逻辑是什么？

sentences.en: He was really influenced by Milton Friedman, a libertarian economiSt.
sentences.zh: 他深受自由意志主义经济学家米尔顿·弗Friedman的影响。

sentences.en: They believed that free trade was a win-win situation, that it would increase our exports, which would create all these jobs, and take away government regulation.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自由贸易是双赢的局面，会增加我们的出口，从而创造所有这些就业机会，并取消政府管制。

sentences.en: And they were deeply opposed to that.
sentences.zh: 他们对此坚决反对。

sentences.en: And Reagan actually managed to take a step towards NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 里根实际上设法朝着北美自由贸易协定迈出了一步。

sentences.en: He had made an agreement with Canada that allowed for goods to be exported without tariffs or duties, and goods to be imported without tariffs or duties.
sentences.zh: 他与加拿大达成了一项协议，允许货物在没有关税或捐税的情况下出口，货物在没有关税或捐税的情况下进口。

sentences.en: Thus, free trade.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就是自由贸易。

sentences.en: Thus, it was called free trade.
sentences.zh: 因此，它被称为自由贸易。

sentences.en: But the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但美国

sentences.en: and Canada had similarly developed economies.
sentences.zh: 和加拿大有着相似的发展经济。

sentences.en: They paid about the same level in wages.
sentences.zh: 他们的工资水平差不多。

sentences.en: The difference with NAFTA was now you were creating a similar agreement with Mexico, with a country that was quite impoverished.
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定的不同之处在于，现在你正在与墨西哥建立类似的协议，这是一个相当贫困的国家。

sentences.en: And the critics immediately feared that it was merely a pretext to allow corporations to exploit cheap labor.
sentences.zh: 批评者立即担心这只是一种借口，允许大公司剥削廉价劳动力。

sentences.en: In other words, they could avoid paying union wages by moving plants to Mexico.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们可以通过将工厂搬到墨西哥来避免支付工会工资。

sentences.en: Mexican workers were paid far less than a unionized Canadian or American worker.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥工人的工资远低于加入工会的加拿大或美国工人。

sentences.en: So in this moment, there's really a philosophical debate occurring.
sentences.zh: 所以在此时此地，确实存在一场哲学辩论。

sentences.en: Will this trade agreement help the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这项贸易协定会帮助美国

sentences.en: economy or will it hurt it?
sentences.zh: 经济还是会损害它？

sentences.en: And the Republicans, from what you're saying, are coming down strongly on the side of this being good for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 照你所说，共和党人强烈支持这对美国

sentences.en: economy and good for the United States in general.
sentences.zh: 经济有利，对整个美国有利。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And it was really George H.W.
sentences.zh: 实际上是乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush who pursued NAFTA and actually negotiated the agreement with his counterparts, the prime minister of Canada and the president of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 布什推行了北美自由贸易协定，并实际上与他的同行——加拿大总理和墨西哥总统谈判了该协议。

sentences.en: However, it still needed to be ratified by Congress and then signed into law by the president.
sentences.zh: 然而，它仍然需要得到国会的批准，然后由总统签署成为法律。

sentences.en: So NAFTA becomes the centerpiece of the 1992 presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 因此，北美自由贸易协定成为1992年总统竞选的核心。

sentences.en: Good evening and welcome to the second of three presidential debates between the major candidates for president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 晚上好，欢迎收看美国总统主要候选人之间的三场总统辩论中的第二场。

sentences.en: There were three candidates, George H.W.
sentences.zh: 当时有三位候选人，乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush, the Republican incumbent versus Democratic nominee Bill Clinton, and then a really interesting third-party candidate named Ross Perot, who was a wealthy businessman.
sentences.zh: 布什（共和党现任总统）对阵民主党候选人比尔·克林顿，还有一个非常有趣的第三方候选人名叫罗斯·佩罗，他是一位富商。

sentences.en: So, President Bush, I think you said it earlier.
sentences.zh: 那么，布什总统，我想你之前说过。

sentences.en: Let's get it on.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 走吧。

sentences.en: George H.W.
sentences.zh: 乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush took the position that the agreement should just be signed.
sentences.zh: 布什的立场是该协议应该直接签署。

sentences.en: The thing that saved us in this global economic slowdown has been our exports.
sentences.zh: 在这次全球经济放缓中拯救我们的是我们的出口。

sentences.en: And what I'm trying to do is increase our exports.
sentences.zh: 我正试图做的是增加我们的出口。

sentences.en: It would lead to an export boom and a great flourishing of American jobs.
sentences.zh: 这将导致出口繁荣和美国就业机会的大发展。

sentences.en: And I won't have more of these free trade agreements.
sentences.zh: 我不会再有更多这样的自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: Ross Perot was the most critical.
sentences.zh: 罗斯·佩罗是最具批判性的。

sentences.en: The most important issue for him was opposition to NAFTA, and he articulated that position.
sentences.zh: 对他来说最重要的议题是反对北美自由贸易协定，他明确表达了这一立场。

sentences.en: If you're paying $12, $13, $14 an hour for factory workers, and you can move your factory south of the border, pay $1 an hour for your labor,
sentences.zh: 如果你支付每小时12、13、14美元给工厂工人，而你可以把工厂搬到边境以南，为你的劳动力支付每小时1美元，

sentences.en: have no health care, have no environmental controls, no pollution controls, and no retirement, and you don't care about anything but making money.
sentences.zh: 没有医疗保健，没有环境控制，没有污染控制，没有退休保障，而且你除了赚钱什么都不在乎。

sentences.en: He issued one of the most memorable lines about NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 他发表了关于北美自由贸易协定最令人难忘的一句话之一。

sentences.en: There will be a giant sucking sound going south.
sentences.zh: 将会有巨大的吸吮声向南传去。

sentences.en: He said that there would be a giant sucking sound of American jobs if NAFTA was passed.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果北美自由贸易协定通过，美国的工作岗位将发出巨大的吸吮声。

sentences.en: I'd like to answer the question because I've actually been a governor for 12 years.
sentences.zh: 我想回答这个问题，因为我实际上已经当了12年州长。

sentences.en: Bill Clinton did something very striking.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿做了一件非常引人注目的事情。

sentences.en: He took a middle position.
sentences.zh: 他采取了中间立场。

sentences.en: So I've known a lot of people who've lost their jobs because of jobs moving overseas, and I know a lot of people whose plants have been strengthened by increasing exports.
sentences.zh: 所以我认识很多人因为工作转移到海外而失业，我也认识很多人他们的工厂因为出口增加而得到了加强。

sentences.en: In which he supported the agreement.
sentences.zh: 他支持该协议。

sentences.en: The trick is to expand our export base and to expand trade on terms that are fair to us.
sentences.zh: 秘诀在于扩大我们的出口基础，并在对我们公平的条款上扩大贸易。

sentences.en: But he wanted separate side agreements to protect environmental regulations and labor.
sentences.zh: 但他希望有单独的配套协议来保护环境法规和劳工。

sentences.en: So more trade, but on fair terms, and favor investment in America.
sentences.zh: 所以要更多的贸易，但在公平的条款上，并赞成在美国投资。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I think we have a question over here.
sentences.zh: 我想我们这里有一个问题。

sentences.en: So Bush, the Republican in the race, he's pretty much saying, do this deal.
sentences.zh: 所以参选的共和党人布什基本上是在说，做这笔交易。

sentences.en: Don't worry about it.
sentences.zh: 不用担心。

sentences.en: It's going to work out.
sentences.zh: 会成功的。

sentences.en: Perot, the independent, is saying, don't do this deal.
sentences.zh: 独立候选人佩罗则在说，不要做这笔交易。

sentences.en: This is a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: It's going to hurt American manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 这会损害美国的制造业。

sentences.en: Clinton, the Democratic nominee, and as we know, future president, he's trying to straddle those two.
sentences.zh: 民主党候选人克林顿，正如我们所知，是未来的总统，他正试图兼顾这两者。

sentences.en: And I want to linger on Clinton.
sentences.zh: 我想继续谈谈克林顿。

sentences.en: Why do you think Clinton took that middle approach, given that the Democratic Party had been the party of organized labor
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么克林顿会采取这种中间路线，鉴于民主党一直是工会组织政党

sentences.en: and had relied on manufacturing workers and their unions as such a core constituency in elections?
sentences.zh: 并将制造业工及其工会视为选举中的核心选民基础？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, the Democrats had been out of power for 12 years.
sentences.zh: 民主党已经下台12年了。

sentences.en: By that point, there was a tremendous desire to reclaim the presidency.
sentences.zh: 到那时，有一种夺回总统宝座的极强烈渴望。

sentences.en: Bill Clinton was also part of what they called the New Democrats, which had emerged in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿也是他们所说的新民主党人的一部分，该党派在80年代崛起。

sentences.en: And it was trying to reorient the party to be more business-friendly, corporate-friendly,
sentences.zh: 它试图重新定位政党，使其对商业更友好、对企业更友好，

sentences.en: and remove its image as a party that was supportive of the activist government of the New Deal, that it had become modernized.
sentences.zh: 摆脱其支持新政激进政府的政党形象，它已经现代化了。

sentences.en: And NAFTA was seen as the future.
sentences.zh: 而北美自由贸易协定被视为未来。

sentences.en: Organized labor was deeply opposed throughout.
sentences.zh: 有组织劳工自始至终坚决反对。

sentences.en: And the reason he tried to find this middle position was to allay their fears and to thread this needle.
sentences.zh: 他试图找到这个中间立场的原因是为了消除他们的担忧并走钢丝。

sentences.en: And for the purposes of this election, he did thread the needle.
sentences.zh: 为了这次选举的目的，他确实走成了钢丝。

sentences.en: He won.
sentences.zh: 他赢了。

sentences.en: However, it's also worth noting that Ross Perot won 19% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 然而，同样值得注意的是，罗斯·佩罗赢得了19%的选票。

sentences.en: That was the highest share since 1912.
sentences.zh: 那是自1912年以来的最高得票率。

sentences.en: For a third-party candidate.
sentences.zh: 对于一个第三方候选人来说。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Bill Clinton is now the president of the United States, the first Democrat in 12 years, and he begins selling NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿现在是美国总统，12年来的第一位民主党人，他开始推销北美自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: I have lived with the manufacturing changes of the last 15 years.
sentences.zh: 我经历过过去15年制造业的变化。

sentences.en: And I would never knowingly do anything that would cost Americans jobs.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会明知故犯地做出任何会牺牲美国人工作岗位的事情。

sentences.en: Mainly to the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 主要是对民主党。

sentences.en: He needed a significant faction of them in order to pass it.
sentences.zh: 他需要他们中的一大部分人才能通过它。

sentences.en: So he pushed very, very hard.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常非常努力地推动。

sentences.en: But I'm telling you, nothing I do as your president within the borders of the United States can create more jobs and higher incomes unless somebody buys the stuff we produce.
sentences.zh: 但我告诉你，作为你的总统，我在美国境内所做的任何事情，除非有人购买我们生产的东西，否则都无法创造更多的工作岗位和更高的收入。

sentences.en: He thought more exports would help create more American jobs, offsetting whatever loss of jobs we would have.
sentences.zh: 他认为更多的出口将有助于创造更多的美国工作岗位，从而抵消我们可能损失的任何工作岗位。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a—the world is changing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个——世界正在改变。

sentences.en: So as cruel or tough as it is, we can't pretend that it's not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，不管它多么残酷或艰难，我们不能假装它不会发生。

sentences.en: You know, there was also an undercurrent of inevitability.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中也有一种不可避免的潜流。

sentences.en: Globalization was here whether we like it or not.
sentences.zh: 无论我们喜欢与否，全球化已经到来。

sentences.en: And we had to tame it to our benefit.
sentences.zh: 而我们必须驯服它，为我们所用。

sentences.en: So I ask you to talk to your friends and neighbors.
sentences.zh: 所以我请你们去和你们的朋友、邻居谈谈。

sentences.en: Talk to the people who are worried about it.
sentences.zh: 去和那些对此感到担忧的人谈谈。

sentences.en: Tell them their fears are well-founded, but they don't have anything to do with this agreement.
sentences.zh: 告诉他们，他们的担忧是有依据的，但这些担忧与这项协议无关。

sentences.en: This agreement will make it better.
sentences.zh: 这项协议会使情况变得更好。

sentences.en: The other thing he does is he dispatches Al Gore, his vice president.
sentences.zh: 他做的另一件事是派出了他的副总统阿尔·戈尔。

sentences.en: Welcome to a special edition of Larry King Live.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看《拉里·金直播》特别节目。

sentences.en: And Gore winds up sitting across from Ross Perot on Larry King Live.
sentences.zh: 结果戈尔在《拉里·金直播》上与罗斯·佩罗针锋相对地坐在一起。

sentences.en: This is a huge—
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大的——

sentences.en: This, I remember.
sentences.zh: 这个，我记得。

sentences.en: This was an event.
sentences.zh: 这是一场大事件。

sentences.en: Huge national event.
sentences.zh: 一场巨大的国家级事件。

sentences.en: And they debate NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 他们在辩论北美自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: When I'm in a room with corporate America, the first thing they say is,
sentences.zh: 当我和美国企业界共处一室时，他们说的第一件事就是：

sentences.en: Perot, why don't you keep your mouth shut?
sentences.zh: 佩罗，你为什么不闭嘴？

sentences.en: Perot is saying his corporate CEO friends are telling him, please shut up.
sentences.zh: 佩罗说，他那些企业CEO朋友们叫他闭嘴。

sentences.en: This is a great deal for us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说是一笔极好的买卖。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Gore is relying heavily on this technocratic expertise.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，戈尔严重依赖这种技术官僚的专业知识。

sentences.en: Every living former president of the United States in both parties, every former secretary of state, every former secretary of treasury,
sentences.zh: 两党所有在世的前美国总统、每一位前国务卿、每一位前财政部长、

sentences.en: every living Nobel Prize winner in economics, conservatives, liberals, everyone in between, they've never agreed on anything.
sentences.zh: 每一位在世的诺贝尔经济学奖得主、保守派、自由派以及中间派的所有人，他们从来没有在任何事情上达成过一致。

sentences.en: He is basically saying this is an empirical fact.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，这是一个经验事实。

sentences.en: There have been 23 studies of the impact of NAFTA on jobs in the United States.
sentences.zh: 已有23项关于北美自由贸易协定对美国就业影响的研究。

sentences.en: Twenty-two of them have shown that it will cause an increase in jobs in the United States.
sentences.zh: 其中22项表明，它将增加美国的就业机会。

sentences.en: It's what the experts say is the best thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是专家们所说的最好的事。

sentences.en: He's saying trust the smartest people in the country.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，相信这个国家最聪明的人。

sentences.en: Trust the smartest people.
sentences.zh: 相信最聪明的人。

sentences.en: And that is also really interesting in terms of the Democratic Party's realignment away from working-class,
sentences.zh: 就民主党从工人阶级、

sentences.en: labor-oriented party towards someone that is really concerned with technocratic advice.
sentences.zh: 劳工导向型政党向真正关心技术官僚建议的政党转型而言，这也是非常有趣的。

sentences.en: And there's another professional class constituency that's deeply in favor.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个专业阶层的选民群体对此深表支持。

sentences.en: That is the media, including the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 那就是媒体，包括《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Our editorial board, we should probably say.
sentences.zh: 也许我们该说，我们的编辑委员会。

sentences.en: Our editorial board.
sentences.zh: 我们的编辑委员会。

sentences.en: A lot of the media were now college-educated folks, and they were distant from these working-class places.
sentences.zh: 许多媒体现在都是受过大学教育的人，他们与这些工人阶级的地方相距甚远。

sentences.en: Organized labor, the people that were fighting NAFTA, were seen as yesterday's news.
sentences.zh: 有组织的劳工，那些反对北美自由贸易协定的人，被视为昨日黄花。

sentences.en: They were fighting a losing battle.
sentences.zh: 他们在打一场注定失败的仗。

sentences.en: NAFTA was the future.
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定代表着未来。

sentences.en: It was irreversible.
sentences.zh: 它是不可逆转的。

sentences.en: There was a lot of triumphalism around this time.
sentences.zh: 那个时期弥漫着一种胜利主义情绪。

sentences.en: It feels like what you're describing is something of an echo chamber, where these Democratic leaders in the Clinton administration
sentences.zh: 感觉你所描述的有点像回音室，克林顿政府中的这些民主党领袖

sentences.en: are talking about how every expert thinks this is the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 在讨论每个专家都认为这是正确的事情。

sentences.en: These journalists are hearing that and saying, well, it must be the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这些记者听到这些后说，嗯，那这一定是一件正确的事。

sentences.en: And the overall message that you're therefore hearing from the news media and the White House is kind of the same, which is, this is the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，你从新闻媒体和白宫听到的整体信息基本上是一样的，那就是，这是一件正确的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, it was an echo chamber.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个回音室。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was still a very unpopular idea among the American public.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这在美国公众中仍然是一个极不受欢迎的想法。

sentences.en: Polling at one point showed that two-thirds of the American public were against it.
sentences.zh: 民意调查一度显示，三分之二的美国公众反对它。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: At the same time, there remained one hugely consequential hurdle to the enactment of NAFTA, and that was the vote in the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，北美自由贸易协定通过的道路上仍然存在一个极其重大的障碍，那就是众议院的投票。

sentences.en: A bill to implement the North American Free Trade Agreement.
sentences.zh: 一项实施北美自由贸易协定的法案。

sentences.en: And I would say it was one of the most important debates as far as contemporary politics.
sentences.zh: 我要说，就当代政治而言，这是最重要的辩论之一。

sentences.en: As a speaker for months, the people of America and its representatives have struggled with the challenge of NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，几个月来，美国人民及其代表一直在与北美自由贸易协定的挑战作斗争。

sentences.en: Is it good or is it bad?
sentences.zh: 它是好是坏？

sentences.en: Will it help to expand our economy or shrink it?
sentences.zh: 它会帮助扩大我们的经济还是收缩经济？

sentences.en: Today, the House must decide.
sentences.zh: 今天，众议院必须做出决定。

sentences.en: And the critics were really heard loudly in the House debate.
sentences.zh: 批评的声音在众议院的辩论中确实听得很清楚。

sentences.en: Corporate America and the big money interests have told us that NAFTA is a good deal.
sentences.zh: 美国企业界和庞大的资本利益集团告诉我们，北美自由贸易协定是一笔好交易。

sentences.en: I don't believe them.
sentences.zh: 我不相信他们。

sentences.en: People like Bernie Sanders, who was an independent at the time, spoke out passionately against it.
sentences.zh: 像伯尼·桑德斯这样当时是独立派的人，发表了充满激情的反对讲话。

sentences.en: Even the administration admits there will be at least 200,000 people who will lose their jobs.
sentences.zh: 甚至政府也承认，至少会有20万人失去工作。

sentences.en: And what are we giving to them?
sentences.zh: 而我们又给了他们什么？

sentences.en: Table scraps.
sentences.zh: 残羹冷炙。

sentences.en: And a lot of Democrats came out in force against it.
sentences.zh: 许多民主党人大举站出来反对它。

sentences.en: Mr. Speaker, this debate comes down to one simple question.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，这场辩论归结为一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: Whose side are you on?
sentences.zh: 你站在哪一边？

sentences.en: One of the leading opponents of NAFTA was David Bonyer, who was from Michigan and was the House
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定的主要反对者之一是大卫·博尼尔，他来自密歇根州，是众议院

sentences.en: Whip.
sentences.zh: 党鞭。

sentences.en: The working people who stand against this treaty don't have degrees from Harvard.
sentences.zh: 反对这项条约的劳动人民没有哈佛的学位。

sentences.en: They don't study economic models.
sentences.zh: 他们不研究经济模型。

sentences.en: But they know when the deck is stacked against them.
sentences.zh: 但他们知道什么时候天平在对他们不利。

sentences.en: They know it's not fair to ask American workers to compete against Mexican workers who earn a dollar an hour.
sentences.zh: 他们知道要求美国工人去和每小时只赚一美元的墨西哥工人竞争是不公平的。

sentences.en: He emphasized the resentment of a lot of working class people towards the elite experts that were telling them that they couldn't understand the possible benefits to them.
sentences.zh: 他强调了许多工人阶级对精英专家的怨恨，这些专家告诉他们，他们无法理解可能带来的好处。

sentences.en: But there were a lot of Democratic representatives that were more favorable to NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 但也有许多更倾向于北美自由贸易协定的民主党众议员。

sentences.en: Understandably, many members of this body and citizens of this country are concerned about job loss.
sentences.zh: 可以理解的是，这个机构的许多成员和这个国家的公民都对失业感到担忧。

sentences.en: I am, too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: I am supporting this agreement because job creation and exports go hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 我支持这项协议，因为创造就业和出口是齐头并进的。

sentences.en: Madam Chairman, I rise in support today.
sentences.zh: 主席女士，我今天起立表示支持。

sentences.en: And in all honesty, a decision of this kind has been a tough call for someone from my region of the country.
sentences.zh: 老实说，对于我这个地区的人来说，做出这样的决定是一个艰难的选择。

sentences.en: The fact is that change is not something to fear.
sentences.zh: 事实是，改变并不是什么可怕的事。

sentences.en: We are sending a message about whether the world's only superpower thinks its best days are in the past or in the future.
sentences.zh: 我们正在传递一个信息：世界上唯一的超级大国认为它的巅峰时期是在过去还是在未来。

sentences.en: NAFTA is neither heaven nor hell.
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定既不是天堂也不是地狱。

sentences.en: It's neither nirvana nor the depths of depression.
sentences.zh: 它既不是极乐世界也不是经济萧条的深渊。

sentences.en: It just makes good sense for America's economic future.
sentences.zh: 它对美国的经济未来来说只是合情合理。

sentences.en: I urge my colleagues to vote for it.
sentences.zh: 我敦促我的同僚们投赞成票。

sentences.en: And then there was the vote.
sentences.zh: 然后就是投票。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 234, the nays are 200, and the bill is passed.
sentences.zh: 在此次投票中，赞成票234票，反对票200票，法案获得通过。

sentences.en: And it passes narrowly, 234 to 200.
sentences.zh: 它以234票对200票险胜。

sentences.en: This is a decisive moment for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 这是民主党的一个决定性时刻。

sentences.en: The vast majority of Republicans voted for NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数共和党人都投了北美自由贸易协定的赞成票。

sentences.en: But it was crucial that Democrats had supported it, more than 100 of them.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于民主党人也支持了它，其中有一百多人。

sentences.en: And Bill Clinton's trade representative later said George Bush could have never passed NAFTA, that it had to have been a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿的贸易代表后来表示，乔治·布什永远无法通过北美自由贸易协定，这必须是一个民主党人来做。

sentences.en: It had to have been Bill Clinton.
sentences.zh: 这必须是比尔·克林顿。

sentences.en: He said no Republican president could have because he couldn't have brought enough Democrats.
sentences.zh: 他说，没有任何一个共和党总统能够做到这一点，因为他无法争取到足够的民主党人。

sentences.en: The Senate soon passed the bill three days later.
sentences.zh: 参议院在三天后很快通过了该法案。

sentences.en: And in early December 1993, Bill Clinton signs NAFTA into law.
sentences.zh: 1993年12月初，比尔·克林顿签署将北美自由贸易协定正式立法。

sentences.en: So, Dan, once NAFTA goes from theoretical and the debate is over into a day-to-day free trade reality across North America, what ends up happening?
sentences.zh: 那么，丹，一旦北美自由贸易协定从理论走向现实，辩论结束，成为北美各地日复一日的自由贸易现实时，最终会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, GDP is increasing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，GDP在增长。

sentences.en: The economy is booming on a lot of levels for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，经济在许多层面上都在蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: But it also launches the free trade juggernaut.
sentences.zh: 但它也开启了自由贸易的巨无霸车轮。

sentences.en: Several years later, Bill Clinton is able to establish permanent normal trade relations with China.
sentences.zh: 几年后，比尔·克林顿得以与中国建立永久正常贸易关系。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, in the United States, a lot of factories are moving overseas.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在美国，许多工厂正在向海外转移。

sentences.en: Between 1997 and 2020, more than 90,000 American plants closed.
sentences.zh: 在1997年至2020年间，超过9万家美国工厂关闭。

sentences.en: Some 5 million manufacturing jobs were loSt.
sentences.zh: 大约有500万制造业工作岗位消失了。

sentences.en: This translated into loss of union jobs and a tremendous rise in income inequality.
sentences.zh: 这转化为工会工作岗位的流失以及收入不平等的巨大加剧。

sentences.en: Most of the benefits for NAFTA were going to wealthier people.
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定的大部分好处都落入了较富裕人群的口袋。

sentences.en: So, while it was a net gain for the country as a whole, it wasn't within the country.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然对整个国家而言这是一个净收益，但在国内并非如此。

sentences.en: In other words, the people that don't have a college degree are hurt by trade deals with low-wage countries.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，没有大学学位的人受到了与低工资国家进行贸易协定的伤害。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's important to remember that more than 60% of the population does not have a college degree.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，重要的是要记住，超过60%的人口没有大学学位。

sentences.en: There was a British behavioral scientist that did a study of wellness, and he found that the psychological toll of losing a job is equivalent to losing your spouse.
sentences.zh: 有一位英国行为科学家做了一项关于幸福感的研究，他发现失业造成的心理打击相当于失去配偶。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, it's no wonder that people feel that their lives have been totally destroyed.
sentences.zh: 所以，难怪人们觉得自己的生活彻底被毁了。

sentences.en: And this pain is concentrated very heavily in a lot of the Rust Belt states, Michigan, Ohio, and my own home state of Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 这种痛苦非常集中在铁锈地带的许多州，比如密歇根州、俄亥俄州以及我自己的家乡威斯康星州，

sentences.en: where we start to see the human and political impacts from NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里开始看到来自北美自由贸易协定的人性和政治影响。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天创作《拼写蜜蜂》和《连字》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: So, Dan, tell us what you have found through all your reporting in Wisconsin about the impacts of NAFTA on workers, jobs, and over time, on the politics of that place.
sentences.zh: 那么，丹，请告诉我们，通过你在威斯康星州的所有报道，你发现北美自由贸易协定对工人、工作岗位以及随着时间的推移对当地政治产生了什么影响。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Wisconsin is one of the places where NAFTA's dark side has really become clear.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州是北美自由贸易协定的阴暗面变得显而易见的地方之一。

sentences.en: Milwaukee, which is the state's biggest city and the industrial center of the state,
sentences.zh: 密尔沃基，作为该州最大的城市和工业中心，

sentences.en: it was once known as the machine shop of the world, produced truck frames, agricultural machinery, motors, industrial controls.
sentences.zh: 曾被称为世界机械厂，生产卡车底盘、农业机械、马达和工业控制器。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's important to understand that deindustrialization was already happening before NAFTA passed.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，重要的是要明白，去工业化在北美自由贸易协定通过之前就已经在发生了。

sentences.en: Between 1979 and 1983, Milwaukee had already lost a quarter of its manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 在1979年至1983年间，密尔沃基已经失去了四分之一的制造业。

sentences.en: And then you have NAFTA, which really accelerated this process.
sentences.zh: 然后又有了北美自由贸易协定，它确实加速了这一进程。

sentences.en: And one of the companies that I paid particular attention to is Masterlock.
sentences.zh: 我特别关注的公司之一是马斯特锁。

sentences.en: Everybody knows their iconic padlocks.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道他们标志性的挂锁。

sentences.en: These are the locks literally you use on your high school locker.
sentences.zh: 这些锁字面意思就是你用在高中储物柜上的那种。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Those combination locks, right.
sentences.zh: 那些密码锁，对。

sentences.en: They've been making locks in Milwaukee since the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 他们自20世纪20年代以来一直在密尔沃基制造锁具。

sentences.en: And the plant was a smaller industrial factory.
sentences.zh: 这家工厂是一个规模较小的工业厂房。

sentences.en: At its peak, it employed about 1,300 people.
sentences.zh: 在其巅峰时期，它雇用了大约1300人。

sentences.en: But everyone I spoke to loved working there.
sentences.zh: 但我交谈过的每个人都很喜欢在那里工作。

sentences.en: It was something that was deeply embedded in the city's sort of industrial consciousness.
sentences.zh: 这已经是这座城市某种工业意识中根深蒂固的一部分。

sentences.en: And after NAFTA passes, they did what a lot of other companies were doing.
sentences.zh: 在北美自由贸易协定通过后，他们做了许多其他公司正在做的事情。

sentences.en: They built a plant in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 他们在墨西哥建立了一家工厂。

sentences.en: In their case, this plant in Nogales was quickly taking jobs from the Milwaukee plant.
sentences.zh: 就他们而言，这家位于诺加利斯的工厂迅速抢走了密尔沃基工厂的工作岗位。

sentences.en: Within a two- or three-year period, 1,000 union positions were sent abroad.
sentences.zh: 在两到三年的时间里，1000个工会职位被送到了海外。

sentences.en: But the plant kept going.
sentences.zh: 但这家工厂仍在继续运转。

sentences.en: And it kept employing people, although on much smaller scale than it used to.
sentences.zh: 它继续雇用人员，尽管规模比以前小得多。

sentences.en: And one of the people that I spent time with recently is a very interesting worker named Chancey AdaMs.
sentences.zh: 我最近花时间相处的人之一是一个非常有趣的工人，名叫钱西·亚当斯。

sentences.en: Chancey, man.
sentences.zh: 钱西，老兄。

sentences.en: What's up?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: How you doing?
sentences.zh: 过得还好吗？

sentences.en: Doing good.
sentences.zh: 挺好的。

sentences.en: And he helped me really understand the impact of NAFTA on him and on the wider community and really on American politics as a whole.
sentences.zh: 他真正帮我理解了北美自由贸易协定对他、对整个社区以及对美国政治整体所产生的影响。

sentences.en: Just start at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我们就从头开始讲吧。

sentences.en: What was it like growing up in Milwaukee when you were—this was like in the 80s and 90s?
sentences.zh: 你在密尔沃基长大的时候是什么样的？大概是80年代和90年代。

sentences.en: It was hard, but it wasn't, if that makes sense, is what I'm trying to say.
sentences.zh: 挺不容易的，但如果这样说能懂的话，其实也没那么糟，这就是我想表达的。

sentences.en: Tell us about Chancey AdaMs.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲钱西·亚当斯吧。

sentences.en: What should we know?
sentences.zh: 我们应该了解他些什么？

sentences.en: Well, Chancey was born in 1980, grew up on the north side of Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，钱西出生于1980年，在密尔沃基北部长大。

sentences.en: I come up in a single family home, so me and my brother, my sister, and my mother.
sentences.zh: 我是单亲家庭长大的，所以家里只有我和我哥、我姐还有我妈。

sentences.en: He was raised by a single mom.
sentences.zh: 他是单亲妈妈抚养长大的。

sentences.en: She was a cook at a Milwaukee museum.
sentences.zh: 她曾是密尔沃基一家博物馆的厨师。

sentences.en: I mean, she's just a hard worker.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她工作极其刻苦。

sentences.en: She went to work and made sure we had everything we needed.
sentences.zh: 她辛勤工作，确保我们拥有所需的一切。

sentences.en: And we came up and never went hungry, never went without clothes or anything, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们长大过程中从未挨过饿，从没缺过衣服什么的，你知道的。

sentences.en: What about the neighborhood you grew up in?
sentences.zh: 那你长大的那个社区呢？

sentences.en: Just describe what it was like when you were a kid.
sentences.zh: 描述一下你小时候那里是什么样的。

sentences.en: It was great to me, you know.
sentences.zh: 对我来说挺棒的，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's like, I grew up on 9th and Burleigh, so there was a lot of bad things going on down there.
sentences.zh: 就像，我在第九街和伯利街交界处长大，所以那片区域发生过很多不好的事情。

sentences.en: It was a lot of drug dealing and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 有很多毒品交易之类的事情。

sentences.en: But I don't have nothing bad to say about where I grew up in my childhood.
sentences.zh: 但我对自己的童年成长地方没有什么不好的评价。

sentences.en: It was good.
sentences.zh: 挺好的。

sentences.en: When you were young, what did you do for fun in the neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 你小时候在社区里都玩些什么？

sentences.en: He described a happy childhood, biking around with his friends.
sentences.zh: 他描述了一个快乐的童年，和朋友们骑着自行车四处闲逛。

sentences.en: I would roll past Madison like a thousand, thousand times as a kid, you know?
sentences.zh: 小时候我骑车经过麦迪逊街大概有上千、上万次吧，你知道吗？

sentences.en: One of the places where they biked around were the plants on the north side of Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 他们骑车闲逛的地方之一就是密尔沃基北部的工厂区。

sentences.en: This was a city that's deeply entwined with its industrial history, and Milwaukee is filled with these factories.
sentences.zh: 这是一座与其工业历史深交织的城市，密尔沃基到处都是这样的工厂。

sentences.en: Miller, Masterlock, Bridges and Stratton, A.L.
sentences.zh: 米勒、马斯特洛克、布里奇斯与斯特拉顿公司，A.L.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: Them was the places where a lot of people from the south came.
sentences.zh: 那些地方是很多南方人来的地方。

sentences.en: Like, my family was Bridges and Stratton and A.L.
sentences.zh: 比如，我的家人就在布里奇斯与斯特拉顿和A.L.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯工作。

sentences.en: Them, the plants they got in.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们进的工厂。

sentences.en: And these are places where Chancey's relatives worked.
sentences.zh: 这些都是钱西的亲戚们工作过的地方。

sentences.en: Growing up, you hear older people talk like, them are the places where you want to be.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，你总听老一辈人说，那些地方就是你想去的地方。

sentences.en: And it was, like, solid, good wage.
sentences.zh: 而且，那工作确实很稳定，工资待遇很好。

sentences.en: Good wage.
sentences.zh: 工资很高。

sentences.en: And, like, you can tell, like, when we was, like, kids, we'd be riding there, and you'd see the cars out there.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以发现，当我们还是小孩子的时候，我们会骑车去那里，然后你会看到那里的汽车。

sentences.en: You'd see all nice cars.
sentences.zh: 你会看到全是好车。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Going to work.
sentences.zh: 开去上班的。

sentences.en: You know, so we knew that was money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以我们知道那里有钱赚。

sentences.en: So, if you was, like, my age then, and you figure, hey, I'm not going to college, but I'm going to, these are one of the jobs that you was going to try to get.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你当时和我差不多大，然后你想，嘿，我不打算上大学，但我要去，这些就是你要努力争取进去的工作之一。

sentences.en: Eventually, a friend of his, who had gotten a job at Masterlock, calls him and says, you know, you should really apply here.
sentences.zh: 最终，他的一个在马斯特洛克找到工作的朋友打电话给他，说，你知道的，你真的应该来这里申请。

sentences.en: Let me try it out.
sentences.zh: 让我去试试吧。

sentences.en: And he actually got me in.
sentences.zh: 而且他真的帮我弄进去了。

sentences.en: So, he applies for a job at Masterlock as a temp and gets one in 2010.
sentences.zh: 于是，他在2010年申请了马斯特洛克的一份临时工工作并成功入职。

sentences.en: Now, Dan, you had said there isn't a ton of Masterlock left after NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 那么，丹，你刚才说过，北美自由贸易协定之后，马斯特洛克已经没剩多少规模了。

sentences.en: So, by the time Chancey gets a job there in 2010, how much of Masterlock is there for him to really join in Milwaukee?
sentences.zh: 所以，到2010年钱西去那里找工作时，密尔沃基的马斯特洛克还剩下多少规模供他真正加入？

sentences.en: There's only a couple hundred union positions at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时只剩下几百个工会岗位了。

sentences.en: Chancey started out at a little more than $10 an hour.
sentences.zh: 钱西刚开始的时薪略高于10美元。

sentences.en: But Chancey talked so much about how immediately he took to it.
sentences.zh: 但钱西多次谈到他是如何迅速适应这份工作的。

sentences.en: You know, I see a lot of these older men and the things they accumulated in life working at this plant and the work they put in.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我看到很多这些老员工，以及他们在工厂工作一生所积累的财富和他们付出的努力。

sentences.en: And I'm like, you know, that's what I want right there.
sentences.zh: 我就想，你知道的，那才是我想要的生活。

sentences.en: For Chancey and a lot of the workers, while the starting wage was low, there was a lot of room for advancement to skilled jobs that paid much, much more.
sentences.zh: 对钱西和许多工人来说，虽然起薪很低，但有很大的晋升空间，可以转到薪水高得多的技术岗位。

sentences.en: How much does Chancey and everyone else among these several hundred workers who are still at Masterlock,
sentences.zh: 钱西以及仍在马斯特洛克的这几百名工人中的其他人，

sentences.en: how much do they worry that what's left of this company would eventually be outsourced under the incentives of NAFTA?
sentences.zh: 他们有多担心这家公司剩下的部分最终会在北美自由贸易协定的驱使下被外包出去？

sentences.en: I think some feared it, but many felt like they were secure.
sentences.zh: 我想有些人很害怕，但许多人觉得他们很安全。

sentences.en: They had highly specialized jobs.
sentences.zh: 他们从事高度专业化的工作。

sentences.en: And there was another reason they felt this sense of security.
sentences.zh: 他们感受到这种安全感还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: Do you remember when President Obama came to the plant?
sentences.zh: 你还记得奥巴马总统来工厂视察的时候吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was my first year there.
sentences.zh: 记得，那是我在那里的第一年。

sentences.en: First or second year.
sentences.zh: 第一年还是第二年。

sentences.en: In 2012, Barack Obama paid a visit to Masterlock.
sentences.zh: 2012年，巴拉克·奥巴马访问了马斯特洛克。

sentences.en: I'm actually here today because this company has been making the most of a huge opportunity that exists right now to bring jobs and manufacturing back to the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 我今天之所以来这里，是因为这家公司充分利用了当前将工作岗位和制造业带回美利坚合众国的巨大机遇。

sentences.en: I knew it wasn't going nowhere.
sentences.zh: 我知道它不会搬走的。

sentences.en: He was there on the strength of how Masterlock was supposed to have been bringing jobs back.
sentences.zh: 他去那里是因为马斯特洛克本该把工作岗位带回来。

sentences.en: By then, Masterlock had increased its Milwaukee workforce to a little more than 300.
sentences.zh: 到那时，马斯特洛克将其密尔沃基的员工人数增加到了300多人。

sentences.en: Some people told me it was because they'd had a few challenges manufacturing overseas.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，这是因为他们在海外制造时遇到了一些挑战。

sentences.en: So there was a modest reshoring, but something that was trumpeted by the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以出现了一次回流，但这成为了美国总统大肆宣扬的政绩。

sentences.en: We're going to create more success stories like Masterlock, and we will remind the world just why it is the United States is the greatest nation on earth.
sentences.zh: 我们将创造更多像马斯特洛克这样的成功故事，我们将向世界重申为什么美国是地球上最伟大的国家。

sentences.en: Thank you, everybody.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: God bless you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你们。

sentences.en: God bless you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你们。

sentences.en: I just happened to be so close.
sentences.zh: 我当时碰巧离得很近。

sentences.en: So when he came off the stage, he was just shaking everybody's hand, and I was right there.
sentences.zh: 所以当他走下舞台时，他一直在跟每个人握手，而我就站在那里。

sentences.en: So I shook his hand in everything.
sentences.zh: 所以我跟他握了手，什么都有。

sentences.en: How did it make you feel?
sentences.zh: 这让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I'm the man.
sentences.zh: 我太牛了。

sentences.en: I mean, you got to think about where I come from, where I come from.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你得想想我是从哪里出来的，我出身于什么环境。

sentences.en: I just shook the president's hand because I didn't really know too much about politics and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚握了总统的手，因为我以前对政治之类的事情其实不太了解。

sentences.en: And I was in the union now, and, you know, I was learning a little bit at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我加入了工会，你知道的，那时我也正在学一点东西。

sentences.en: And for Chancey, this is a big moment.
sentences.zh: 对于钱西来说，这是一个重大的时刻。

sentences.en: He had never been politically active, but he had started getting involved with the union.
sentences.zh: 他以前从未积极参与过政治，但他开始参与工会事务。

sentences.en: And here he is, meeting the president of the United States, who the union is heavily supporting.
sentences.zh: 而现在他在这里，见到了受到工会全力支持的美国总统。

sentences.en: So I voted.
sentences.zh: 所以我投票了。

sentences.en: And he votes for the first time in his life for Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 他人生中第一次投票投给了巴拉克·奥巴马。

sentences.en: He the man.
sentences.zh: 他太了不起了。

sentences.en: They called me Obama at the plant because I was the first black guy to run the hydromats at Mashalot.
sentences.zh: 他们在工厂里叫我奥巴马，因为我是第一个在马斯特洛克开液压组合机（hydromat）的黑人小伙。

sentences.en: And he starts moving up at the plant.
sentences.zh: 他在工厂里开始步步高升。

sentences.en: He learns to operate a complex machine called a hydromat.
sentences.zh: 他学会了操作一台名为液压组合机的复杂机器。

sentences.en: And now he's making $20 an hour.
sentences.zh: 现在他的时薪达到了20美元。

sentences.en: He's working a lot, sometimes seven days a week, making a lot of overtime.
sentences.zh: 他工作很拼，有时一周干七天，赚了很多加班费。

sentences.en: And he buys his first house.
sentences.zh: 他买下了自己的第一栋房子。

sentences.en: When I met the guy over here I bought the house from, he used to work at Mashalot.
sentences.zh: 当我遇到这边卖给我房子的那个人时，他以前也在马斯特洛克工作过。

sentences.en: And I got my keys and all of that.
sentences.zh: 我拿到了钥匙以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And I sat on my stairs over here, and I cried.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那边的楼梯上，哭了起来。

sentences.en: Because, like, I'm sitting on these stairs right now.
sentences.zh: 因为，就像我现在正坐在这个楼梯上一样。

sentences.en: I'm sitting on my sweat right now.
sentences.zh: 我坐在这里感受着自己的血汗。

sentences.en: I worked hard.
sentences.zh: 我努力工作了。

sentences.en: And I bought my first house.
sentences.zh: 我买下了我的第一栋房子。

sentences.en: And I bought it at $35 or something.
sentences.zh: 我是用3.5万左右买下的。

sentences.en: By myself.
sentences.zh: 靠我自己的力量。

sentences.en: Eventually, he's earning more than $30 an hour.
sentences.zh: 最终，他的时薪超过了30美元。

sentences.en: And not only is his job at Masterlock helping him grow a nest egg and support his family, he's got four kids.
sentences.zh: 不仅他在马斯特洛克的工作帮他积攒了一笔财富并养家糊口，他还拥有四个孩子。

sentences.en: But it's a real source of pride for him.
sentences.zh: 但这对他来说也是真正的骄傲之源。

sentences.en: My mother was very, my sister and brother, they're very proud of it.
sentences.zh: 我母亲非常骄傲，我姐和我哥，他们都为此感到骄傲。

sentences.en: My brother work now.
sentences.zh: 我哥现在有工作了。

sentences.en: He said one of the things that gets him up in the morning knowing that I'm up in the morning.
sentences.zh: 他说让他早晨醒来的动力之一，就是知道我也在早晨醒来。

sentences.en: I know little bro up.
sentences.zh: 我知道小弟弟醒了。

sentences.en: I know he going to work.
sentences.zh: 我知道他要去上班。

sentences.en: Oh, let me get up.
sentences.zh: 哦，我也得起床了。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: Man, it's a beautiful feeling to be the little brother and have everybody look up to your work ethic.
sentences.zh: 天哪，作为一个弟弟，能让所有人敬佩你的职业道德，这种感觉真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: And seeing where you come from and seeing what you're accumulating.
sentences.zh: 看着你出身的地方，看着你所积累的成就。

sentences.en: I did become a man in that plant.
sentences.zh: 我确实在那家工厂里真正成长为一个男人。

sentences.en: But it made me realize I'm a good man.
sentences.zh: 但这让我意识到我是一个好人。

sentences.en: I feel good about myself.
sentences.zh: 我对自己的感觉很好。

sentences.en: I feel good going to work every day and coming in and the younger guys looking at me, how I looked at the older guys when I was coming in young.
sentences.zh: 我每天去上班、走进工厂时感觉很好，年轻小伙子们看着我，就像我当年刚进厂时看着老员工那样。

sentences.en: They see me in my uniform.
sentences.zh: 他们看到我穿着制服。

sentences.en: They see me, you know, with a nice haircut, smelling good.
sentences.zh: 他们看到我，你知道的，发型很精神，身上香香的。

sentences.en: They know that it's strictly sweat that's got me what I got.
sentences.zh: 他们知道我拥有的一切完全是靠血汗换来的。

sentences.en: So it makes you feel great.
sentences.zh: 所以这让你感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I wasn't going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我可没打算去别的地方。

sentences.en: Tell me about May 24th, last year.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲去年5月24号那天吧。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the day, it was a normal day.
sentences.zh: 那天刚开始的时候，是个普通的日子。

sentences.en: The supervisor, he came to us and said, we have a town hall.
sentences.zh: 主管来到我们这说，我们要开个全员大会。

sentences.en: So we go upstairs.
sentences.zh: 于是我们上楼去。

sentences.en: But the whole scenery was different.
sentences.zh: 但整个现场的布置完全不同了。

sentences.en: Like, the chairs was turned a certain way.
sentences.zh: 比如，椅子朝向了特定的方向。

sentences.en: It was tables, like, barricaded.
sentences.zh: 摆了桌子，就像设置了路障一样。

sentences.en: And it was armed guards up there.
sentences.zh: 上面还有带枪的警卫。

sentences.en: So I'm like, whoa, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，哇，这是怎么了？

sentences.en: And he announced it.
sentences.zh: 然后他宣布了消息。

sentences.en: I have some bad news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个坏消息要宣布。

sentences.en: I'm here to inform y'all of March of 24, the plant will be closing.
sentences.zh: 我来这里通知大家，3月24日，工厂将要关闭。

sentences.en: And the whole room was silent.
sentences.zh: 整个房间顿时鸦雀无声。

sentences.en: No explanation.
sentences.zh: 没有任何解释。

sentences.en: No nothing.

sentences.zh: 几个人站起来走了出去。

sentences.zh: 有些女士哭了起来。

sentences.en: Some men were just angry.
sentences.zh: 有些男士则是满腔愤怒。

sentences.en: Some guys said, I knew it.
sentences.zh: 有些小伙子说，我早就知道了。

sentences.en: I knew it.
sentences.zh: 我早就知道了。

sentences.en: What were you feeling when you heard the news?
sentences.zh: 听到这个消息时你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I went numb.
sentences.zh: 我当时整个人都麻木了。

sentences.en: And then I got a sense of being scared.
sentences.zh: 接着我感到一阵恐惧。

sentences.en: I put my whole life around this place.

sentences.zh: 我现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: I'm 43 years old.

sentences.en: So 30 years after NAFTA passed, the Masterlock plant in Milwaukee is finally closing.
sentences.zh: 在北美自由贸易协定通过30年后，密尔沃基的马斯特洛克工厂终于要关门了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's the final chapter on the Milwaukee story of Masterlock.
sentences.zh: 这是密尔沃基与马斯特洛克故事的最终章。

sentences.en: Some of these jobs will go to other places.
sentences.zh: 其中一些工作会转移到其他地方。

sentences.en: But one union official told me that most of them will go to the company's plant in Nogales, Mexico.
sentences.zh: 但一位工会官员告诉我，大部分工作将转移到该公司位于墨西哥诺加莱斯的工厂。

sentences.en: So what happens to Chancey?
sentences.zh: 那么钱西会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Well, Chancey is really in a kind of desperate state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，钱西现在的处境确实可以说是陷入了绝境。

sentences.en: He's scrambling.
sentences.zh: 他在四处奔波。

sentences.en: No one wanted to hire me.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意雇我。

sentences.en: He applies for jobs.
sentences.zh: 他到处申请工作。

sentences.en: Nothing is coming through.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有着落。

sentences.en: But then a co-worker at Masterlock gets him a job at another factory.
sentences.zh: 但后来马斯特洛克的一位同事帮他在另一家工厂找到了工作。

sentences.en: But he's making a lot less than what he used to at Masterlock.
sentences.zh: 但他现在的收入比在马斯特洛克时少得多。

sentences.en: So I had to get another job.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不去找另一份工作。

sentences.en: I was going to lose my house.
sentences.zh: 我差点失去房子。

sentences.en: So he eventually picks up a second job.
sentences.zh: 所以他最终还是找了一份兼职。

sentences.en: Yeah, they'll get there by 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 对，他们会在早上5点到那儿。

sentences.en: Now his days start very early.
sentences.zh: 现在他的日子从很早就开始了。

sentences.en: Whenever I get done.
sentences.zh: 无论我什么时候下班。

sentences.en: So usually about 9 o'clock, 9.30.
sentences.zh: 所以通常大概是9点、9点半吧。

sentences.en: And very late.
sentences.zh: 而且结束得很晚。

sentences.en: And then have to come right home and try to eat something, jump into bed, and get up again at 3.45.
sentences.zh: 然后不得不立刻回家，试着吃点东西，倒头就睡，紧接着3点45分又要起床。

sentences.en: He hardly has any time for himself except a little bit on the weekends.
sentences.zh: 除了周末能有一点时间外，他几乎没有属于自己的时间。

sentences.en: So it's a constant moving, constant grind, constant no sitting down.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一直在奔波，一直在苦熬，一刻也不能坐下来。

sentences.en: And it's tiring, you know, mentally, really.
sentences.zh: 而且真的很累，你知道的，从精神上来说。

sentences.en: I keep thinking back to the Democrats on the House floor who warned that this is what was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我不禁回想起众议院里那些民主党人，他们曾警告说事情会变成这样。

sentences.en: And for a time in listening to you tell this story about Chansey, it feels that he's the exception.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，听你讲钱西的故事时，会觉得他是个特例。

sentences.en: You know, he's not going to be hurt by NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他不会被北美自由贸易协定伤害。

sentences.en: But it feels like one of the morals of this story is that NAFTA kind of comes for almost everyone when it comes to these plants in the upper MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 但感觉这个故事的教训之一是，当谈到中西部上游的这些工厂时，北美自由贸易协定几乎会波及到每个人。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 对，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: And there's so many ways that NAFTA has shifted the power balance.
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定在许多方面改变了权力平衡。

sentences.en: You know, we talked a lot about the closing of these plants.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们讨论了很多关于这些工厂关闭的事。

sentences.en: But it's also true that NAFTA gave companies enormous leverage even just to threaten to close the plant.
sentences.zh: 但同样真实的是，北美自由贸易协定赋予了公司巨大的筹码，甚至只是威胁要关闭工厂。

sentences.en: And that they could extract steep concessions on unions and others to lower their wages.
sentences.zh: 他们可以向工会和其他人榨取苛刻的妥协条件，以降低工资。

sentences.en: It's a real downward pressure on working class Americans.
sentences.zh: 这对美国工人阶级构成了实实在在的向下压力。

sentences.en: We talked about this a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们之前讨论过这个。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确认一下。

sentences.en: So you're not planning to vote this year.
sentences.zh: 所以你今年不打算投票了。

sentences.en: Nah, I'm done with that.
sentences.zh: 不，我受够了。

sentences.en: It's pointless.
sentences.zh: 毫无意义。

sentences.en: I haven't benefited off of nothing that any president had ever done.
sentences.zh: 历任总统做过的事我一点好处都没捞到。

sentences.en: It's always been taken from me.
sentences.zh: 我拥有的总是一直在被剥夺。

sentences.en: If you're poor or right in the middle of poor and middle class, you're going to bust your ass, man, to get what you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你很穷，或者刚好处于贫困和中产阶级之间，老兄，你得拼死拼活才能得到你想要的东西。

sentences.en: There's no help.
sentences.zh: 没有任何帮助。

sentences.en: That's why I have no respect for politics, presidents, and it changed me.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我对政治和总统毫无敬意，这改变了我。

sentences.en: Do you have any thoughts on Trump or Kamala Harris?
sentences.zh: 你对特朗普或卡玛拉·哈里斯有什么看法吗？

sentences.en: Yes, Trump is a crook, but he's gangster.
sentences.zh: 对，特朗普是个骗子，但他是个狠角色。

sentences.en: I love that guy.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢那家伙的。

sentences.en: He don't care.
sentences.zh: 他毫不在乎。

sentences.en: The only good thing I can say about Trump is he's a businessman.
sentences.zh: 我能对特朗普说的唯一好话就是他是个商人。

sentences.en: He'll be successful that way, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他在那方面会成功。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris, she's just a crook.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯，她也就是个骗子。

sentences.en: Everybody keep getting on this black wave, black wave, because they're black.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在赶这股黑色浪潮，黑色浪潮，就因为他们是黑人。

sentences.en: You should've fucked my own.
sentences.zh: 我本该支持我自己人。

sentences.en: I don't care what color you are.
sentences.zh: 我才不管你是什么肤色。

sentences.en: You suck.
sentences.zh: 你太烂了。

sentences.en: You suck.
sentences.zh: 你太烂了。

sentences.en: I definitely have no faith in her.
sentences.zh: 我对她绝对没有信心。

sentences.en: If I wasn't to vote and I had to choose between the two, I would vote for Trump.
sentences.zh: 如果我不去投票，但又必须在这两者之间二选一，我会投特朗普。

sentences.en: At the beginning of our conversation,
sentences.zh: 在我们对话刚开始的时候，

sentences.en: you talked about this idea that NAFTA and its aftermath turned the Democrats from the party of the working class into the party of college-educated elites.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了这样一个观点：北美自由贸易协定及其后果，把民主党从工人阶级的政党变成了受过大学教育的精英政党。

sentences.en: Which helps me understand, in a way I don't think I ever really did before, just how much of an opening Republicans had to remake themselves into the party that exploits that.
sentences.zh: 这让我以一种以前从未真正有过的理解方式认识到，共和党人有多大的空间把自己重塑为利用这一点的政党。

sentences.en: And that obviously comes in the candidacy of Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 而这显然体现在唐纳德·特朗普的参选上。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Free trade is the mantra of both parties.
sentences.zh: 自由贸易是两党共同的咒语。

sentences.en: It's what's coming out of Washington until the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 直到2016年大选之前，华盛顿传出的都是这个声音。

sentences.en: I'm going to say something that conservatives don't like.
sentences.zh: 我要说一些保守派不喜欢的话。

sentences.en: Because while I'm a free trader, I'm a smart trader.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然我支持自由贸易，但我支持的是明智的贸易。

sentences.en: I'm a fair trader.
sentences.zh: 我支持公平贸易。

sentences.en: I know what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 我知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Donald Trump emphasized an economic nationalist message.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普强调了经济民族主义的信息。

sentences.en: And you're losing plants over here.
sentences.zh: 这边的工厂在倒闭。

sentences.en: And you're losing a plant over there.
sentences.zh: 那边的工厂在倒闭。

sentences.en: Highlighting the job losses from NAFTA and other free trade deals.
sentences.zh: 突显了北美自由贸易协定和其他自由贸易协定造成的失业问题。

sentences.en: Any direction I can point to, you're losing jobs, you're losing your plants.
sentences.zh: 我指出的任何方向，你都在失去工作，失去工厂。

sentences.en: We're not going to let it happen anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们再也不会让这种事发生了。

sentences.en: So now you have an incredible shift in the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 所以现在共和党发生了难以置信的转变。

sentences.en: The party that created NAFTA in the first place is now opposed to it, at least rhetorically.
sentences.zh: 最初创建北美自由贸易协定的政党现在却反对它，至少在口头上是这样。

sentences.en: And of course, the Democratic candidate he faces is none other than Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 当然，他面对的民主党候选人正是希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: Your husband signed NAFTA, which was one of the worst things that ever happened to the manufacturing industry.
sentences.zh: 你丈夫签署了北美自由贸易协定，这是对制造业发生的最糟糕的事情之一。

sentences.en: And in the presidential debates, NAFTA becomes one of the most important issues.
sentences.zh: 在总统辩论中，北美自由贸易协定成为了最重要的问题之一。

sentences.en: NAFTA is the worst trade deal, maybe ever signed anywhere, but certainly ever signed in this country.
sentences.zh: 北美自由贸易协定是有史以来签署的最糟糕的贸易协定，也许在任何地方都是，但绝对是在这个国家签署的。

sentences.en: And now...
sentences.zh: 现在……

sentences.en: Trump rails against it, calls it the worst deal ever made.
sentences.zh: 特朗普对此大加挞伐，称这是有史以来最糟糕的协议。

sentences.en: I think my husband did a pretty good job in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 我认为我丈夫在20世纪90年代做得相当不错。

sentences.en: I think a lot about what worked and how we can make it work again.
sentences.zh: 我经常思考什么行之有效，以及我们如何能让它再次行之有效。

sentences.en: Well, he approved NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他批准了北美自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: But Clinton largely defends it.
sentences.zh: 但克林顿大体上在为它辩护。

sentences.en: Which is the single worst trade deal ever approved in this country.
sentences.zh: 这是该国历史上批准的唯一最糟糕的贸易协定。

sentences.en: Incomes went up for everybody.
sentences.zh: 所有人的收入都增加了。

sentences.en: What was it, do you think, in this debate and in this campaign that made Hillary Clinton and the Democrats so confident that NAFTA, opposition to it,
sentences.zh: 你认为，在这场辩论和竞选中，是什么让希拉里·克林顿和民主党人如此确信，北美自由贸易协定以及对它的反对，

sentences.en: was a losing strategy for Trump?
sentences.zh: 对特朗普来说是一场注定失败的策略？

sentences.en: Because clearly she could have mimicked his position.
sentences.zh: 因为很明显，她本可以模仿他的立场。

sentences.en: She could have said, you know, we've come a long way and I think that NAFTA did have some real probleMs.
sentences.zh: 她本可以这样说：你知道的，我们已经走了很长一段路，我认为北美自由贸易协定确实存在一些真正的问题。

sentences.en: Well, I think she made a political calculation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为她做了政治算计。

sentences.en: It was really articulated very well by Senator Chuck Schumer in the summer of 2016 in the lead-up to the election.
sentences.zh: 这在2016年夏天大选临近前，由参议员查克·舒默表达得非常清楚。

sentences.en: He said, for every blue-collar Democrat we lose in western Pennsylvania, we will pick up two moderate Republicans in the suburbs of Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们在宾夕法尼亚州西部每失去一个蓝领民主党人，我们就会在费城郊区争取到两个温和的共和党人。

sentences.en: And you can repeat that in Ohio, in Illinois, in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 你可以在俄亥俄州、伊利诺伊州、威斯康星州重复这一点。

sentences.en: Can you just translate that?
sentences.zh: 你能翻译一下吗？

sentences.en: What is he saying about NAFTA's impact on the politics of the parties?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么评价北美自由贸易协定对两党政治的影响的？

sentences.en: I think he's signaling a class realignment of the party.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是在发出该党阶级重组的信号。

sentences.en: They are going to focus their efforts on winning suburban voters who tend to be wealthier versus the blue-collar workers that had traditionally supported the party since the New Deal.
sentences.zh: 他们将把精力集中在争取那些往往更富裕的郊区选民上，而不是自新政以来一直支持该党的蓝领工人。

sentences.en: That's kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: So what Democrats are saying explicitly, and it sounds like an on-the-record quote, is we recognize that we have now become a party whose appeal is to higher-income,
sentences.zh: 所以民主党人明确表示，这听起来像是一句官方引言，我们认识到我们现在已经成了一个吸引高收入、

sentences.en: higher-educated Americans.
sentences.zh: 受教育程度更高的美国人的政党。

sentences.en: And we may be forsaking a certain kind of working-class voter in western Pennsylvania or Wisconsin, and we're okay with that because we think the math favors us.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会抛弃宾夕法尼亚州西部或威斯康星州的某种工人阶级选民，我们觉得没关系，因为我们认为数学上的赢面偏向我们这边。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And this kind of thinking was so embedded in Hillary Clinton's campaign that she didn't visit Wisconsin once during the general election.
sentences.zh: 这种想法在希拉里·克林顿的竞选团队中根深蒂固，以至于她在整个大选期间一次都没有去过威斯康星州。

sentences.en: In the end, Trump wins the presidency very narrowly by flipping three of the so-called blue-wall states, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 最后，特朗普以微弱优势赢得总统大选，通过翻转被称为“蓝墙”三个州中的三个：密歇根州、宾夕法尼亚州和威斯康星州。

sentences.en: This is something no Republican had done in more than 30 years.
sentences.zh: 这是30多年来没有哪个共和党人做到过的事情。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's a surprise that these states were some of the hardest hit by NAFTA and similar free trade agreements.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些州是受北美自由贸易协定及类似自由贸易协定打击最重的地区之一，这绝非巧合。

sentences.en: And Trump did renegotiate NAFTA in 2018 with the United States-Mexico-Canada agreement.
sentences.zh: 特朗普确实在2018年通过《美墨加协定》重新谈判了北美自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: It made modest improvements in conditions for Mexican workers to disincentivize the movement of jobs and factories to Mexico.
sentences.zh: 它对墨西哥工人的工作条件进行了适度改善，以打消工作岗位和工厂向墨西哥转移的积极性。

sentences.en: But it doesn't seem as though that's worked.
sentences.zh: 但似乎这并没有起作用。

sentences.en: Last year, for example, Stellantis, one of the big three, moved some production to a plant in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 例如，去年，三大汽车制造商之一的斯泰兰蒂斯将部分生产转移到了墨西哥的一家工厂。

sentences.en: And, of course, Masterlock has closed its Milwaukee factory.
sentences.zh: 当然，马斯特洛克也关闭了其密尔沃基工厂。

sentences.en: But on paper and kind of symbolically to voters, Trump did fulfill a pledge to go after the original NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 但在纸面上，以及在对选民的象征意义上，特朗普确实履行了针对最初的北美自由贸易协定的承诺。

sentences.en: That is true, and that is what he's campaigning on.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，这也是他竞选的卖点。

sentences.en: Like a lot of Trump's promises, they didn't really ever come through.
sentences.zh: 就像特朗普的许多承诺一样，它们从未真正兑现。

sentences.en: And he actually passed tax cuts that incentivized offshoring of jobs.
sentences.zh: 他实际上通过了鼓励工作岗位外包的减税政策。

sentences.en: On the Democratic side, you had also a real realignment.
sentences.zh: 在民主党这边，你也经历了一次真正的重组。

sentences.en: President Biden and Vice President Harris increased the tariffs that Trump had established on certain Chinese products, such as electric vehicles.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统和哈里斯副总统提高了特朗普对某些中国产品（如电动汽车）确立的关税。

sentences.en: Biden has also emphasized his closeness to labor unions in a way that previous Democrats for generations had not.
sentences.zh: 拜登还以几代人之前的民主党人所没有的方式，强调了他与工会的亲密关系。

sentences.en: And he's really courted them and was the first president to walk on the picket line, which is very significant when you think back on the NAFTA debate.
sentences.zh: 他确实极力拉拢他们，并且是第一位走上罢工纠察线的总统，当你想起当年的北美自由贸易协定辩论时，这意义重大。

sentences.en: And Bill Clinton is pushing aside the concerns of organized labor.
sentences.zh: 而比尔·克林顿则将有组织劳工的关切抛在一边。

sentences.en: We should point out that this is a somewhat meaningful thing for Biden to do because he was in the Senate when NAFTA passed.
sentences.zh: 我们应该指出，这对拜登来说是一件颇有意义的事情，因为北美自由贸易协定通过时他在参议院。

sentences.en: He voted for NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 他投票支持了北美自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: He did vote for NAFTA, and he voted for the agreement establishing permanent normal trade relations with China.
sentences.zh: 他确实投了赞成票，而且他还投票支持了与中国建立永久正常贸易关系的协议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Dan,
sentences.zh: 丹，

sentences.en: it feels like Biden's journey here is emblematic of the journey of the entire Democratic Party because what you have by the end of Biden's presidency is a situation where Democrats who brought NAFTA over the line and really gave us our current free trade era under Bill Clinton,
sentences.zh: 感觉拜登的这段心路历程正是整个民主党心路历程的缩影，因为到拜登总统任期结束时，情况变成了这样：当年在比尔·克林顿手下把北美自由贸易协定推过终点线、并真正把我们带入当前自由贸易时代的民主党人，

sentences.en: and then who watched Republicans exploit the fallout from it under Donald Trump, Democrats now themselves have said, you know what, this all went too far.
sentences.zh: 后来又眼睁睁看着共和党人在唐纳德·特朗普的带领下利用其带来的余波，而如今民主党人自己也说，你知道吗，这一切都走得太远了。

sentences.en: And Biden and the Democrats, I'm sure, probably wouldn't put it this way, but their rhetoric now on free trade, on things like NAFTA, has moved a lot closer to Trump's.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，拜登和民主党人可能不会这样表述，但他们现在关于自由贸易、关于北美自由贸易协定之类的言论，已经比以往任何时候都更接近特朗普了。

sentences.en: And I have to believe that's because they now recognize what NAFTA did to the working class.
sentences.zh: 我不得不相信，那是因为他们现在认识到了北美自由贸易协定对工人阶级做了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 对，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: And by the time we enter this campaign, both parties are critical of the free trade agreements of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当我们进入这次竞选时，两党都对过去的自由贸易协定提出了批评。

sentences.en: Kamala Harris, one of her first events with Tim Walz, was at a UAW hall in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯与蒂姆·沃尔兹的首次活动之一，就是在密歇根州的一个全美汽车工人联合会大厅。

sentences.en: And she has really emphasized the importance of good paying jobs, whether it's too little or too late is an open question.
sentences.zh: 她确实强调了高薪工作的重要性，但这究竟是为时过早还是为时已晚，还是个未知数。

sentences.en: You're talking about 50 years of deindustrialization and that was greatly accelerated and intensified by NAFTA and the free trade deals that followed it.
sentences.zh: 你谈到的是长达50年的去工业化进程，而这一进程被北美自由贸易协定及随后的自由贸易协定大大加速和加剧了。

sentences.en: If you could say anything to Trump or Kamala Harris about your life and your experiences with Masterlock growing up in Milwaukee, what would you tell them?
sentences.zh: 如果你能对特朗普或卡玛拉·哈里斯谈谈你的生活以及你在密尔沃基长大、在马斯特洛克的经历，你会对他们说些什么？

sentences.en: What would you want them to know?
sentences.zh: 你希望他们知道些什么？

sentences.en: One of the main things you people need to do is keep these jobs in the United States, man.
sentences.zh: 你们这些人需要做的最主要事情之一，就是把这些工作留在美国，老兄。

sentences.en: These are people's livelihoods.
sentences.zh: 这些都是人们的生计。

sentences.en: People get up and go to work every day, not even getting paid what they're worth.
sentences.zh: 人们每天早起上班，得到的报酬甚至配不上他们的付出。

sentences.en: To eat, and then they snatch it.
sentences.zh: 好不容易吃上饭，然后就被抢走了。

sentences.en: They take it away with ease.
sentences.zh: 他们轻而易举地把东西夺走。

sentences.en: And the people that's taking it away is well off.
sentences.zh: 而那些巧取豪夺的人却过着优渥的生活。

sentences.en: They don't have to worry about these struggles.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不用担心这些挣扎。

sentences.en: I think it tells a larger story of American working class disaffection that's rooted in a response to NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了美国工人阶层更大的不满情绪，这种情绪根源于对北美自由贸易协定的反应。

sentences.en: That response isn't always rational or linear.
sentences.zh: 这种反应并不总是理性的或线性的。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's unpredictable.
sentences.zh: 有时它是不可预测的。

sentences.en: Trump seized on that, making wild promises that appealed to a lot of people in desperate times.
sentences.zh: 特朗普抓住了这一点，在绝望的时期许下了迎合许多人的狂热承诺。

sentences.en: The Democrats have started to shift away from that, focusing more on what I think is the most underappreciated issue in American politics.
sentences.zh: 民主党人已经开始摆脱这种做法，更多地关注我认为是美国政治中最被低估的问题。

sentences.en: And it's so simple and almost banal, but it's really jobs, and it's particularly well-paying jobs.
sentences.zh: 这很简单，几乎有点陈词滥调，但其实就是工作，特别是高薪工作。

sentences.en: And what that means to a person that doesn't have a college degree, that sense that they're okay, and their family's okay,
sentences.zh: 这对一个没有大学学历的人意味着什么，那种觉得他们自己没问题、家人也没问题的感觉，

sentences.en: and who's the best person that's going to help make those jobs and give them this opportunity.
sentences.zh: 以及谁才是最能帮助创造这些工作并给他们提供机会的人。

sentences.en: Well, Dan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，丹，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: It was really a pleasure talking with you.
sentences.zh: 和您交谈真是一件愉快的事。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: By Monday night, Hurricane Milton had strengthened at an explosive pace, becoming a lethal Category 5 storm with winds of 180 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 到周一晚上，飓风“米尔顿”以惊人的速度增强，演变成一场致命的五级风暴，风速达到每小时180英里。

sentences.en: It's just an incredible, incredible, incredible hurricane.
sentences.zh: 这真是一场难以置信、难以置信、难以置信的飓风。

sentences.en: Milton is expected to make landfall on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: “米尔顿”预计将于周三登陆。

sentences.en: Its exact path is still taking shape, but forecasters predict it will bring life-threatening wind, rain, and flooding to coastal Florida,
sentences.zh: 其确切路径仍在形成中，但预报员预测它将给佛罗里达州海岸带来致命的风、雨和洪灾，

sentences.en: where local meteorologist John Morales of NBC News was briefly overcome with emotion as he tried to capture the storm's scale.
sentences.zh: 在那里，NBC新闻的当地气象学家约翰·莫拉莱斯在试图描述这场风暴的规模时，一度情绪激动。

sentences.en: It has dropped 50 millibars in 10 hours.
sentences.zh: 它在10小时内气压下降了50毫巴。

sentences.en: I apologize.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: This is just horrific.
sentences.zh: 这简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: The maximum sustained winds are 160.
sentences.zh: 最大持续风速为160。

sentences.en: Florida officials have ordered evacuations across at least 12 counties and have suspended tolls in order to keep traffic moving as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州官员已下令至少12个县进行疏散，并暂停收费，以使交通尽可能快地通行。

sentences.en: What would you say to people tonight who are saying, you know what, I'm going to ride this out, I've ridden others out.
sentences.zh: 你会对今晚那些说“你知道吗，我要硬扛过去，我以前也经历过”的人说些什么？

sentences.en: What would you say to people who aren't heeding those evacuation orders?
sentences.zh: 你会对那些不听从疏散命令的人说些什么？

sentences.en: I can say without any dramatization whatsoever, if you choose to stay in one of those evacuation areas, you're going to die.
sentences.zh: 我可以毫不夸张地说，如果你选择留在这些疏散区之一，你就会死。

sentences.zh: 哇。
